newsitem.title: USA: Casino America ends dispute, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Casino America ends dispute, sees charge.

text.p: Casino America Inc said Friday that it has resolved a dispute with the Louisiana Gaming Control Board and the Louisiana State Police and as a result will pay about $8 million, including interest.
The company said it would charge about half the amount against its operations for the fourth quarter ending April 30.

The dispute involved the deductibility of double jackpots at the company's Isle of Capri Casinos in Bossier City and Lake Charles, Louisiana, for purposes of determining the amount of gaming tax owed.

Casino America said it would capitalize the remaining half of the amount it will pay as additional purchase price related to its acquisition of the minority interests in these two Louisiana casino operations in 1996.

Casino America owns and operates five riverboat and dockside casinos. These include the Isle of Capri Casino in Biloxi, Mississippi; the Isle of Capri Casino in Vicksburg, Mississippi; the Isle of Capri Casino in Bossier City, Louisiana; and two riverboats operating at the Isle of Capri Casino in Lake Charles, Louisiana.
